title: Release Preflight Signal Library & Readiness Checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, practical signal library + readiness checklist intended for Product Ops and Release Leads to rapidly assess whether a release is fit for incremental rollout. It leans on lightweight quantitative signals (KPIs) plus qualitative gates (docs, support readiness). Designed to live as a shared sheet during the shiproom and be exported into sprint notes or the release playbook.

How to use this sheet (quick):
- Before shiproom: owners populate current values for each signal, add short notes if any outliers.
- During shiproom: run the readiness score (bottom of sheet) and mark any blocking items; assign action owners and ETA.
- Post-approval: snapshot the sheet into the release artifact (Confluence page link above) and create follow-ups for any amber/red items.

Signal categories (columns in sheet):
- Signal ID: short key, e.g., S-OPS-01.
- Signal name: human-friendly.
- Type: metric | doc | infra | staffing | compliance.
- Target / Gate rule: pass/fail or threshold (e.g., error rate < 0.3%).
- Current value: numeric or short text.
- Trend: up | down | flat (last 7d).
- Owner: person/team responsible.
- Impact level: low | medium | high (est. user/business impact).
- Blocker? yes/no.
- Notes & mitigation: short text.

Core signals (suggested rows) — mix of product ops/KPI/ops readiness:
1) S-KPI-01: Critical path APDEX (30s p95 for main route) | Type: metric | Gate: p95 < 30s | Owner: eng-sre | Impact: high | Blocker if failing.
2) S-KPI-02: Token cost forecast delta | Type: metric | Gate: +10% vs baseline = amber | Owner: product-hosted-api | Impact: medium.
3) S-OBS-03: Error rate (500/4xx) for target route | Type: metric | Gate: < 0.5% | Owner: observability | Impact: high.
4) S-SEC-01: External audit checklist applied (PII flows reviewed) | Type: compliance | Gate: yes | Owner: security-and-compliance | Impact: high.
5) S-DOC-01: Support playbook drafted and on-call runbook created | Type: doc | Gate: yes | Owner: customer-success | Impact: high.
6) S-ROLL-01: Canary traffic plan defined + rollback criteria | Type: doc | Gate: yes | Owner: product-ops | Impact: high.
7) S-ENG-01: DB schema migrations backwards compatible | Type: infra | Gate: yes | Owner: platform-engineering | Impact: high.
8) S-QA-01: Regression test coverage for top-5 flows | Type: metric | Gate: >= 90% pass | Owner: release-engineering | Impact: medium.
9) S-DD-01: Data retention & telemetry budget configured for release | Type: infra | Gate: yes | Owner: infra | Impact: medium.
10) S-CS-01: Known customer blocking issues list empty | Type: doc | Gate: empty | Owner: customer-success | Impact: high.

Readiness scoring (simple):
- Each signal = 0 (fail), 0.5 (amber), 1 (pass).
- Weighted by Impact: low=0.8, medium=1.0, high=1.2.
- Readiness score = sum(signal_score * weight) / sum(max_weight_per_signal). Normalize to 0-100.
- Quick thresholds: >=90 green (go), 70-89 amber (conditional go with mitigations), <70 red (no rollout).

Automated checks to wire in (recommended):
- Pull last 24h and 7d metrics for error rate, latency p95, and token cost forecast via Grafana API.
- Verify feature flag state via LaunchDarkly/FF provider for canary gate alignment.
- Confirm Schema migration status via DB migration job output (CI job).
- Confirm release pipeline artifacts built (SHA + Docker image present).

Playbook items for amber/red signals:
- Immediate triage owner assigned in shiproom (owner must have ETA <= 8h for high-impact items).
- If blocker is infra/perf: limit canary to 1% traffic and enable short TTL fallback.
- If blocker is docs/support: no canary until support playbook complete (except internal-only experiment).
- If blocker is security/compliance: pause rollout until security sign-off.

Common gotchas (notes from past releases):
- Metric drift: token cost delta often looks fine initially then grows after week 1. Precompute 14d rolling estimate.
- Observability gaps: missing service-level tags cause partial dashboards; require checklist entry to validate tag coverage.
- Over-optimistic error sampling: run a raw log sample query for the last 1000 requests to validate.

Release day checklist (quick):
- [ ] Shiproom sign-off recorded in this sheet (name + timestamp).
- [ ] Canary plan deployed (flags + routing).
- [ ] On-call rotation confirmed and pager rule tested.
- [ ] Support playbook link shared to #cs-release channel.
- [ ] Rollback procedure tested in staging and smoke-tested.
- [ ] Telemetry alerts on for deviations (error rate, latency).

Post-release monitoring windows & owner handoff:
- T+0-2h: eng-sre and product-ops watch; focus on error rate and 95th latency.
- T+2-24h: product owner + customer-success review usage; log urgent escalations.
- T+24-72h: collect quality regressions and create follow-up tickets for any >3% regression in core metrics.

Column templates to add to sheet (suggested tabs):
- Signals (master): the list above + free form.
- Signal history: daily snapshots of key metrics for trend charts.
- Actions & owners: auto-filtered open actions from shiproom.
- Rollout log: timestamped entries (who approved, % traffic, notes).
- Postmortem triggers: quick boolean checks that flip when thresholds crossed.

Open questions / decisions to make before adopt as canonical product-ops artifact:
- Do we enforce a mandatory performance gate (p95) for every release or only for performance-impacting changes?
- Which team owns the readiness score validation pipeline (product-ops vs release-engineering)?
- Is a single unified sheet OK, or do we split by release type (hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private)?

Quick links (for copying into sheet cells):
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PROD/launch-framework
- Release checklist template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PROD/standard-release-template
- Grafana dashboard: grafana.redwood.ai/d/ops-release/latency-and-errors

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally terse; the goal is a readable scan during shiproom. If this lands as canonical, we should add small scripts to fetch metric values and compute the readiness score automatically.
- I recommend a 2-week pilot using 5 internal releases (non-customer-facing) to validate false positive/negative rate of the gating rules before adopting for enterprise launches.
